Rashi on Pesachim 43b:10:1.english: I have only all of it - When the entire burning [on the altar] is of leaven.

Rashi on Pesachim 43b:10:2.hebrew: מקצתו - חצי זית שאינו הקטר שלם, דאין הקטרה פחותה מכזית:
Rashi on Pesachim 43b:10:2.english: Part of it - Half an olive-bulk, which is not a complete burning, as a burning is not less than an olive-bulk.

Rashi on Pesachim 43b:10:3.hebrew: עירובו מניין - כשאינו בעין, אלא מעורב ונבלל עם מנחה הוגנת של מצות לאחר שפתתן, דאינן בעין:
Rashi on Pesachim 43b:10:3.english: Its mixture, from where? - When it is not intact [on its own], rather mixed and mingled with a valid meal-offering of unleavened [loaves] after he crumbled them, so that they are not discernible.

Rashi on Pesachim 43b:12:1.hebrew: אין היתר מצטרף לאיסור - אכל חצי זית חלב וחצי זית בשר בבת אחת, אין היתר משלים את שיעור האיסור לחייבו. חוץ מאיסורי נזיר, שאם אכל חצי זית ענבים וחצי זית לחם בבת אחת, חייב; שהרי אמרה תורה "משרת ענבים לא ישתה" — חייב על שריית פתו ביין, ואי איכא מיין לחודה כזית, למה לי קרא? "וכל משרת" לא גרסינן. ואית דגרסי ליה, ומפרשי דאפילו לרבנן דלא דרשי "כל", "וכל" דרשי. ולא היא, דהא פרכינן לקמן: האי מיבעיא ליה לכדתניא, "משרת" ליתן טעם כעיקר. ואם איתא, נימא ליה: אנא טעמא דידי מ"וכל"! אלא ממשמעותא ד"משרת" נפקא ליה, ו"כל" לא דריש:
Rashi on Pesachim 43b:12:1.english: A permitted [substance] does not join together with a prohibited [substance] - [If one] ate half an olive-bulk of forbidden fat [chelev] and half an olive-bulk of [kosher] meat at the same time, the permitted [food] does not complete the [minimum] measure of the prohibited [food] to make him liable. Except for the prohibitions of a nazirite, where if he ate half an olive-bulk of grapes and half an olive-bulk of bread at the same time, he is liable; for the Torah said, "anything soaked in grapes he shall not drink" (Numbers 6:3) — he is liable for soaking his bread in wine, and if there were an olive-bulk from the wine alone, why would I need a verse? We do not have the reading "vekhol mishrat" [in the Gemara]. There are those who do read it [that way], and explain that even according to the Rabbis who do not expound "kol" ("any"), they do expound "vekhol" ("and any"). But this is not [correct], for we ask below: "This [word] is needed for that which was taught [in a baraita]: 'mishrat' [comes] to render flavor like the substance itself." And if it were so, let him say to him: "I [derive] my reason from 'vekhol'!" Rather, he derives it from the plain implication of "mishrat," and he does not expound "kol."

Rashi on Pesachim 43b:13:1.hebrew: אף שאור בל תקטירו - נמי היתר מצטרף לאיסור. חצי זית קומץ דשאור וחצי זית דמצה, ואינן מעורבין אלא כל אחד ניכר:
Rashi on Pesachim 43b:13:1.english: Also leaven, you shall not burn [it] - Here too, permitted [food] combines with prohibited [food]: half an olive-bulk [of the] handful of leaven and half an olive-bulk of matzah, and they are not mixed together, rather each one is distinct.

Rashi on Pesachim 43b:14:1.hebrew: כר"א דדריש כל - לעיל. ומהתם נפקא ליה, כדאמרן לעיל: מקצתו מניין? ת"ל כל. ודריש ליה הכי: מקצתו מניין — חצי זית שאור וחצי זית מצה עמו:
Rashi on Pesachim 43b:14:1.english: In accordance with Rabbi Eliezer, who derives [from] kol - [as mentioned] above. And from there he [Ze'eiri] derives it, as we said above: "From where [do we know] part of it? The verse states: kol ['any']." And he expounds it thus: "From where [do we know] part of it?" — half an olive-bulk of leaven and half an olive-bulk of unleavened bread with it.

Rashi on Pesachim 43b:1:1.hebrew: מצות עשה שהזמן גרמא - נפקא לן בפ"ק דקידושין (דף כט.) דנשים פטורות:
Rashi on Pesachim 43b:1:1.english: A time-bound, positive mitzva - We derive in the first chapter of Kiddushin (29a) that women are exempt.

Rashi on Pesachim 43b:1:2.hebrew: קמ"ל - האי כל, דמוזהרות על החמץ. וכיון דמוזהרות על לאו דחמץ, חייבות בעשה דאכילת מצה לילה הראשון, ואע"ג דזמן גרמא, כר' אליעזר. הואיל וישנן בבל תאכל חמץ, דנפקא לן מכל אוכל חמץ, ישנן בקום אכול מצה:
Rashi on Pesachim 43b:1:2.english: It teaches us - [through] this [word] "anyone," that [women] are warned against [eating] leavened bread. And since they are warned against the negative commandment of leavened bread, they are obligated in the positive commandment of eating matzah [on] the first night, even though [it is] time-bound, in accordance with Rabbi Eliezer: since they are included in "you shall not eat leavened bread," which is derived for us from "anyone who eats leavened bread," they are included in "arise [and] eat matzah."

Rashi on Pesachim 43b:4:1.hebrew: קאי באוכלין - כל דגבי כרת באוכלי חמץ כתיב, אבל כל דאזהרה בנאכל כתיב, "כל מחמצת":
Rashi on Pesachim 43b:4:1.english: Dealing with those who eat - [The word] "kol" [anyone] regarding karet is written in reference to those who eat leavened bread, whereas [the word] "kol" [any] of the prohibition is written in reference to that which is eaten: "anything leavened."

Rashi on Pesachim 43b:4:2.english: It is dealing with those who eat, [and] includes things that are eaten - [This is said] as a rhetorical question.

Rashi on Pesachim 43b:5:1.english: Which [one] offers - [This] implies consecrated [animals], and that they [must] be unblemished.

Rashi on Pesachim 43b:6:1.hebrew: התם דליכא לרבויי אוכלין - דהא נשים מדרב יהודה נפקי, השוה הכתוב אשה לאיש לכל עונשין שבתורה:
Rashi on Pesachim 43b:6:1.english: There, where there are no eaters to include - For women are derived from [the statement of] Rav Yehuda: "Scripture equated a woman to a man for all punishments in the Torah."

Rashi on Pesachim 43b:6:2.hebrew: הכא דאיכא לרבויי אוכלין - דנשים באיסור חמץ, דלא נפקי לן מדרב יהודה כדאמרן לעיל, לא שביק אוכלין ומרבה נאכלין:
Rashi on Pesachim 43b:6:2.english: Here, where there is [room] to include eaters - [namely,] women in the prohibition of chametz, since we do not derive [them] from [the teaching of] Rav Yehuda, as we said above — [the verse] does not leave aside eaters and include things eaten.

Rashi on Pesachim 43b:6:3.hebrew: ופרכינן ורבנן - דפליגי אדר"א בעירוב דחמץ, כיון דלית להו לאו בעירוב, פשיטא, כל דכתיב גבי אזהרה דכל מחמצת לא דרשי. והשתא על כרחך, כל דגבי כרת לרבויי נשים נמי לא דרשי, ואלא נשים מנא להו:
Rashi on Pesachim 43b:6:3.english: And we ask: And the Rabbis - who disagree with Rabbi Eliezer regarding a mixture of chametz, since they do not hold [that there is] a negative prohibition for a mixture, it is obvious [that] "any," which is written regarding the warning of "anything leavened," they do not expound. And now, perforce, they also do not expound "any" regarding karet to include women; so from where do they [derive the obligation for] women?

Rashi on Pesachim 43b:7:1.hebrew: כל - דגבי אזהרה, דלא כתיב "כי" בהדיה, לא דרשינן לרבויי נאכלין דעירובו; אבל גבי כרת דאוכלין, כתיב "כי כל אוכל", דרשינן ליה:
Rashi on Pesachim 43b:7:1.english: Anything [kol] - For regarding the prohibition, where "ki" [for] is not written alongside it, we do not expound [kol] to include foods [eaten] in its mixture; however, regarding karet for those who eat, [where] "ki kol okhel" [for anyone who eats] is written, we do expound it.

Rashi on Pesachim 43b:9:1.hebrew: ומקשינן ור"א אימא כל - דכרת לרבויי נשים, כי כל דכרת לרבויי עירובו נמי לכרת, דכיון דליכא תו אוכלין לרבויי, מרבינן ביה נאכלין כדאמרן גבי חלב, ואימא על עירובו בכרת:
Rashi on Pesachim 43b:9:1.english: And we ask: And [according to] Rabbi Eliezer, say "kol" - [i.e.,] of karet, [is] to include women, [and] "ki kol" of karet [is] to include its mixture as well for karet; for since there are no more eaters to include, we include through it things that are eaten, as we said regarding chelev, and [thus] say [that one is liable] to karet for its mixture.

Tosafot on Pesachim 43b:10:1.hebrew: אין לי אלא כולו מקצתו מנין - בפרק כל המנחות באות מצה (מנחות נח.), מפרש אביי: "אין לי אלא כולו" — דהיינו כזית, "מקצתו" — חצי זית, מניין. ורבא אמר התם דה"ק: אין לי אלא קומץ כולו, מקצת קומץ מניין. ומסיק התם דאיכא בינייהו: דאביי סבר דיש קומץ בפחות מב' זיתים, דהיינו כזית, לכך מפרש "כולו" כזית; וסבר נמי דיש הקטרה בפחות מזית. ואע"ג דבפ' כיצד צולין (לקמן פסחים עט.) א"ר יהושע: "כל הזבחים שבתורה שנשתייר מהן כזית בשר וכזית חלב — זורק את הדם", משמע דאין הקטרה בפחות מכזית — הכא היינו טעמא: משום דסבר דיש קומץ בפחות מב' זיתים, א"כ כשריבה הכתוב חצי קומץ, ע"כ ריבה חצי זית. ורבא סבר: אין קומץ בפחות מב' זיתים, ואין הקטרה בפחות מזית:
Tosafot on Pesachim 43b:10:1.english: "I would have [derived] nothing other than an entire [piece of leaven]; from where [do I derive] part of it?" - In the chapter [entitled] Kol HaMenachot Ba'ot Matzah (Menachot 58a), Abaye explains: "I would have [derived] nothing other than an entire [piece]" — that is, an olive's bulk; "[and] part of it" — half an olive's bulk, "from where [is it derived]?" And Rava said there that this is what [the baraita] means: "I would have [derived] nothing other than an entire handful [kometz]; from where [do I derive] part of a handful?" And [the Gemara] concludes there that there is [a practical difference] between them: for Abaye holds that a handful can be less than two olives' bulk, that is, one olive's bulk, and therefore he explains "an entire [piece]" as an olive's bulk; and he also holds that burning on the altar [haktarah] applies to less than an olive's bulk. And even though in the chapter [entitled] Keitzad Tzolin (later, Pesachim 79a), Rabbi Yehoshua said: "Any of the sacrifices in the Torah from which an olive's bulk of flesh and an olive's bulk of fat remained, [the priest] sprinkles the blood," implying that there is no burning on the altar for less than an olive's bulk — here, this is the reason: because [Abaye] holds that a handful can be less than two olives' bulk, if so, when Scripture included half a handful, it perforce included half an olive's bulk. And Rava holds: there is no handful of less than two olives' bulk, and there is no burning on the altar of less than an olive's bulk.

Tosafot on Pesachim 43b:10:2.hebrew: מאן שמעת ליה דדריש כל ר' אליעזר - אף על גב דר"ע נמי דריש כל בפ' התערובות (זבחים פב.) גבי "כל חטאת", לא קשה; דאפילו יהא כר"ע, מ"מ לא מישתמיט תנא למימר (שיסבור) שיהא תערובת חמץ בכרת. ועוד נראה לר"י, דאפילו לרבנן דלא דרשי הכא "כל", דרשי בעלמא בריש מרובה (ב"ק סג.) דאמר "כל" רבויא הוא, ובפ' שני דסוכה (דף כח.) גבי "כל האזרח"; ודווקא הכא לא דרשי בדבר שאין סברא לרבות, כגון עירובו, וכגון נשים משום היקשא, וכגון מקצת דבל תקטירו. וה"פ: כמאן? כר"א, דדריש "כל" אפילו לדבר שאין סברא לרבות, כגון עירובו וכגון נשים; ואהא קאמר נמי דרבנן לא דרשי "כל":
Tosafot on Pesachim 43b:10:2.english: "Whom did you hear who derives [halakhot from] kol? Rabbi Eliezer" - Even though Rabbi Akiva also expounds kol in the chapter HaTa'arovot (Zevachim 82a) regarding "kol chatat" [any sin-offering], [this] is not difficult; for even if [the baraita] were in accordance with Rabbi Akiva, nevertheless no tanna is ever found to say (that he holds) that a mixture of chametz is [liable] to karet. And furthermore, it appears to the Ri [Rabbeinu Yitzchak] that even according to the Rabbis who do not expound kol here, they do expound [it] elsewhere, in the beginning of [the chapter] Merubeh (Bava Kamma 63a), where [the Gemara] says [that] kol is an inclusion, and in the second chapter of Sukkah (28a) regarding "kol ha-ezrach" [every native-born]. And specifically here they do not expound [it] with respect to a matter where there is no logical reason to include [it], such as its mixture, and such as women because of the heikesh [scriptural juxtaposition], and such as part [of leaven] with respect to "you shall not burn" [bal taktiru]. And this is the explanation [of the Gemara]: Like whom? Like Rabbi Eliezer, who expounds kol even for a matter where there is no logical reason to include [it], such as its mixture and such as women; and it is regarding this too that [the Gemara] says that the Rabbis do not expound kol.

Tosafot on Pesachim 43b:12:1.hebrew: חוץ מאיסורי נזיר - אע"ג דחטאת נמי קאמר לקמן לרבי יוחנן היתר מצטרף לאיסור, הכא לא חשיב חטאת, דבקדשים לא קמיירי:
Tosafot on Pesachim 43b:12:1.english: Except for the prohibitions of a nazirite - Although [regarding] a sin-offering as well, [the Gemara] states later according to Rabbi Yoḥanan [that] a permitted [substance] joins together with a prohibited [substance], here it does not list a sin-offering, because it is not dealing with consecrated [foods].

Tosafot on Pesachim 43b:14:1.hebrew: כמאן? כר"א דדריש "כל" - נראה לר"י דזעירי משמע ליה דשאור היתר מצטרף לאיסור, מדקתני: "עירובו מניין? ת"ל 'כי כל'"; ומדרבי עירובו, א"כ היתר מצטרף לאיסור. והיינו כדרבא, דלדידיה ה"פ: "מקצתו מניין?" — היינו זית שלם. אבל לאביי, דמפרש "מקצתו מניין" — חצי זית, לא שייך היתר מצטרף לאיסור, דאמשהו דאיסור לחודיה מיחייב; והא דמרבה עירובו, היינו כשמתערב לגמרי, ולא אמר שיתבטל האיסור אגב ההיתר. והא דקאמר "כמאן? כר"א דדריש כל", משום דלרבנן, אף על גב דדרשי "כי כל", לא מוקמא ליה לרבות עירובו, אלא לרבות מקצתו. ורש"י פירש דזעירי משמע ליה מקצת — היינו חצי זית קומץ דשאור וחצי זית דמצה, ואין מעורבין, אלא כל אחד ניכר. וק"ל לפירושו טובא: חדא, דלא הוי זעירי לא כאביי ולא כרבא. ועוד, מאי קאמר "כמאן? כר"א"? הא כרבנן נמי אתיא, דהא "כי כל" דרשי, ומוקמינן ליה אמקצתו, דהיינו היתר מצטרף לאיסור לפ"ה! ועוד, בחמץ מנ"ל תערובת, כיון דצריך קרא להיתר מצטרף לאיסור? ועוד, דלפ"ה צ"ל: "מקצתו מניין?" פי' חצי זית איסור וחצי זית היתר שאינם מעורבים יחד, דאי לאו הכי היינו עירוב; ולקמן גבי חטאת משמע דאין היתר מצטרף לאיסור אם לא שיתערב האיסור וההיתר יחד, דהא אמר "עד שיבלע בבשרה":
Tosafot on Pesachim 43b:14:1.english: In accordance with whose [opinion]? In accordance with Rabbi Eliezer, who derives [from] kol - It appears to the Ri [Rabbi Yitzchak] that [regarding] Ze'eiri, it is understood by him that [in the case of] leaven, a permitted substance joins together with a prohibited substance, from that which [the Baraita] teaches: "From where [do we derive] its mixture? Scripture states: 'for any [ki kol]'" — and since it includes its mixture, if so, a permitted substance joins together with a prohibited substance. And this is in accordance with Rava, for according to him this is its explanation: "From where [do we derive] part of it?" — that is, a whole olive-bulk. But according to Abaye, who explains "From where [do we derive] part of it?" [as referring to] half an olive-bulk, [the principle that] a permitted substance joins together with a prohibited substance is not relevant, since one is liable for a minute amount of the prohibited substance by itself; and that which [Scripture] includes its mixture refers to when it is completely mixed together, so that one does not say that the prohibited substance is nullified in the permitted substance. And that which [the Gemara] says, "In accordance with whose [opinion]? In accordance with Rabbi Eliezer, who derives [from] kol," is because according to the Rabbis, even though they [also] derive [from] ki kol, we do not establish it to include its mixture, but rather to include part of it. And Rashi explained that [regarding] Ze'eiri, it is understood by him [that] "part" means half an olive-bulk of a handful of leaven and half an olive-bulk of unleavened bread, and they are not mixed together, rather each one is distinct. And we have many difficulties with his explanation: First, Ze'eiri would be in accordance with neither Abaye nor Rava. Furthermore, what does [the Gemara] mean by saying "In accordance with whose [opinion]? In accordance with Rabbi Eliezer"? Surely it also accords with the Rabbis, for they [too] derive [from] ki kol, and we establish it on "part of it," which is [the case of] a permitted substance joining together with a prohibited substance according to this explanation! Furthermore, regarding chametz, from where would we derive a mixture, since a verse is needed [merely] for a permitted substance joining together with a prohibited substance? Furthermore, according to this explanation, one must say [that] "From where [do we derive] part of it?" means half an olive-bulk of prohibited substance and half an olive-bulk of permitted substance that are not mixed together — for if not so, that would be a "mixture" — whereas later, regarding a sin-offering, it is implied that a permitted substance does not join together with a prohibited substance unless the prohibited substance and the permitted substance are mixed together, for [the Gemara] says: "until it is absorbed in its meat."

Tosafot on Pesachim 43b:1:1.hebrew: סלקא דעתך אמינא כל שישנו בקום אכול מצה - תימה לר"י: היכי סלקא דעתך למידרש הכי? אדרבה, איפכא יש לדרוש, דלחומרא מקשינן! ואור"י דס"ד דאורחיה דקרא דסיפא מפרש לרישיה, משום הכי אמר דבאכילת מצה תלוי דכתיבא בסוף. ועוד יש לומר דהכא יש לדרוש יותר היתר לנשים, משום ג"ש דט"ו מחג הסוכות, והוו מיפטרי ממצה כמו מסוכה, דפטר להו בהדיא בפ' הישן (סוכה כח.) מהלכה למשה מסיני. יש מקשים: למה נשים אין חייבות בציצי', משום דכל שישנו בלבישת שעטנז ישנו בגדילים, כדדרשינן בערכין (דף ג:) גבי כהנים, ולפירוש ר"י דפי' דמסיפא לרישא סברא לדרוש, קשה להפך, שלא יהו נשים חייבות בכלאים! וכי תימא ה"נ? והא בפ"ק דביצה (דף יד:) משמע דכלאים לא חזו למידי:
Tosafot on Pesachim 43b:1:1.english: "It could enter your mind to say [that] anyone included [in the obligation] to arise and eat matzah [is included in the prohibition against eating chametz]" - This is astonishing to R. Yitzchak: How could it enter your mind to expound thus? On the contrary, one ought to expound the opposite, for we make a comparison toward stringency! And R. Yitzchak says that it would enter your mind [to say] that it is the way of Scripture that the latter part [of a verse] explains the first part; therefore, it said that [the prohibition] depends on eating matzah, which is written at the end. And furthermore, one can say that here it is more [reasonable] to expound a leniency for women, because of the gezerah shavah of "the fifteenth" from the Festival of Sukkot, such that they would be exempt from matzah just as [they are exempt] from sukkah, where [the Gemara] explicitly exempts them in the chapter [entitled] HaYashen (Sukkah 28a) based on a law [given] to Moses at Sinai. Some ask: Why are women not obligated in tzitzit? Because [the rule is that] anyone included in wearing sha'atnez is included in [the mitzvah of] fringes, as we expound in Arakhin (3b) regarding priests; yet according to the explanation of R. Yitzchak, who explained that it is logical to expound from the latter part to the first part, there is a difficulty in the reverse — that women should not be obligated in kilayim! And if you say, "Indeed, that is so!" — why, in the first chapter of Beitzah (14b) it is implied that kilayim are not fit for anything!
